html:
SMTO-EXE-0195 — This PDF form has fields with the same name

GUID: 4854ba1b-f4ec-5152-8785-08be7707fbec
Slug: pdf-form-field-ambiguous
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • Two or more fill-in boxes in this PDF form share the same name, so SMTO can't tell them apart. This also happens when combining PDFs whose forms use the same field names. Nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list the PDF's form fields so you can see which names appear more than once. Knowing the repeated names tells you exactly which fields need fixing.
  2. In a PDF editor that can edit forms, give each repeated field its own name and save a copy. If you asked SMTO to add a field, pick a name the form doesn't use yet. With unique names, SMTO knows which box each value belongs in.
  3. If you were combining PDFs, fill in each form and flatten it in a PDF editor (turn the boxes into plain text), or rename the matching fields. Then ask SMTO again. Combining forms that share field names would mix up their answers, so SMTO refuses.

What success looks like

  • SMTO fills or combines the PDF and reports the new PDF it created.

If it still fails

  • Fill in the form by hand in a PDF reader. If you need SMTO to do it, select Copy error details and send them, with the PDF, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • PDF form handling found duplicate fully qualified field names, a field name over 128 characters, a repeated node in the field tree, a new field whose name already exists, or a merge/insert whose sources share field names.

What this means

  • Form enumeration/filling found duplicate fully qualified field names, an overlong unsupported field identity, or merging sources would create duplicate field names. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • Form enumeration/filling found duplicate fully qualified field names, an overlong unsupported field identity, or merging sources would create duplicate field names.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect fully qualified field names and all merge sources; visible labels do not prove distinct field identities.

How to fix it

  • Run pdf.form_fields to see the conflicting names. Use a source whose fully qualified field names are unique and at most 128 characters; give form_field_create a name not already in the document; for merge or insert_pages, rename the colliding fields or flatten the forms in a PDF editor first. Labels cannot be used to select fields.
  • Use a document with unique fully qualified field names. Labels and duplicate names cannot select a mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a document with unique fully qualified field names. Labels and duplicate names cannot select a mutation.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported document has unique valid field identities before form mutation or merge.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
